title: Level 2 (Intermediate) - D-5
notes:
West leads the ♠10 against 3NT. South must hope that the club finesse is working so that 5 club tricks will be available. 2 spade tricks, the ♥A, and the ♦A will bring South's total up to 9 tricks. South could win the first trick with the ♠A, ♠K, or ♠Q, but if South wins with the wrong card the contract will be defeated.

Suppose, for example, that dummy's ♠Q wins the first trick.

East plays low on the first round of clubs, but he covers with the ♣K on the second round as South wins the ♣A. The blockage in clubs prevents South from winning more than 3 tricks in that suit, leaving the contract with no hope. Note that East could have played the ♣K on the first round of the suit, leading to a similarly hopeless position for declarer.

Winning the 1st trick with South's ♠K will lead to the same result, but if South wins trick 1 with dummy's ♠A, the contract will be secure as long as the club finesse works. East covers with the ♣K on the second round of the suit (it would not have helped him to play the ♣K on the first round instead) and South wins the ♣A. South can now unblock the clubs and return to the ♠K to enjoy 2 more club winners.
